assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting changed how trade theory and empirics are done. The framework moved the field beyond representative-firm models and gave new channels for the gains from trade. It is now the workhorse of international trade, and the Melitz model and its extensions are used in macro and policy analysis. It complements the earlier Nobel for new trade theory without duplicating it.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central contribution. Helpman's work on trade with differentiated products, firm-level models and later heterogeneous-firm and labour-market extensions makes him a natural co-recipient. Redding is a major contributor on quantitative and spatial applications but is the more derivative third name. Two laureates give the cleanest attribution.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of confirmation across theory, structural estimation and policy work. It is well tested and well within the usual award horizon.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would rather credit the Krugman-style lineage or the later quantitative-trade lineage (B037) as the core.
Redding's and others' contributions are excluded and could be seen as under-credited.
My assessment relies on general knowledge; I have not independently verified citations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kiyotaki-Moore (1997) is the foundational account of how collateral constraints amplify and propagate shocks. It gives a precise general-equilibrium mechanism for credit cycles and is the basis of a very large literature on financial frictions in macroeconomics, including post-2008 work. The contribution is deep in theory and highly influential for modelling and policy.
assessment.attribution: The central paper is jointly authored by two people, so the attribution is clean. Gertler and Gilchrist are important on the financial accelerator and its empirics, but the Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist lineage is partly covered by the 2022 prize to Bernanke. I would limit the proposal to the dynamic collateral-constraint contribution.
assessment.maturity: Nearly thirty years of use, with confirmation through the global financial crisis and large-scale quantitative macro-finance work.
uncertainties: Possible overlap in the committee's mind with the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises.
How to weigh the Gertler-Gilchrist line against the Kiyotaki-Moore line.
I have not verified citation or award-history details beyond general knowledge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Methods for estimating demand in differentiated-product markets (BLP) and for dynamic industry models (Ericson-Pakes) turned empirical industrial organisation into a quantitative discipline. They are used throughout antitrust, merger analysis, trade and health economics. This is a case where a method-building contribution has changed practice well beyond its home field.
assessment.attribution: Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes are the BLP authors, and Pakes also led the dynamic-games and entry-exit work. Bresnahan, Reiss and others are important adjacent figures, but the three-person limit points to the BLP core. The attribution is coherent but leaves out some contributors.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of widespread use, with applications in policy and in practice.
uncertainties: Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard, Levin and others would be omitted.
The committee may prefer a pure-theory or identification contribution over a method with many applications.
My knowledge may understate recent critiques of the BLP approach.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Persson and Tabellini put the study of political institutions, electoral rules and fiscal outcomes on a rigorous economic footing, in both theory and comparative empirics. The work is widely used in public economics, growth and macro, and it complements the 2024 prize on institutions and prosperity without overlapping it directly.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the core, through their joint books and papers on constitutions and policy outcomes. Besley is a major figure on state capacity and political agency but is a more separate strand. Two names keep the prize focused.
assessment.maturity: Developed over thirty years, with a large follow-on empirical literature and well-established textbook status.
uncertainties: Possible perceived overlap with the 2024 institutions prize.
Whether the committee sees political economics as a single discovery or as a body of work.
Besley's omission may look like an attribution gap.
Persson's role in the Academy and committee community may raise conflict-type questions, which I disclose but do not adjudicate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The task-based view of technology and the China-shock evidence reshaped understanding of how technology and trade affect wages, regional labour markets and politics. The research is influential in both academic and policy debates and combines credible empirical design with clear conceptual framing.
assessment.attribution: Autor is the central figure across the task and trade-shock literatures. Hanson is the strongest partner on local labour market effects of trade. Dorn and Katz are important co-authors, and the task framework also draws on contributions outside this list, so attribution is somewhat diffuse.
assessment.maturity: Roughly fifteen to twenty years of work, with early results re-examined and broadly confirmed, though magnitudes and interpretation are still debated.
uncertainties: The 2024 and 2021 prizes cover adjacent territory in institutions and empirical methods.
The long-run persistence of the China-shock effects is still contested.
Task-based theory is partly attributable to people outside the listed names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hsieh-Klenow (2009) offered a tractable, quantitative way to measure the aggregate cost of input misallocation across firms. It reframed cross-country income differences as partly a question of resource allocation, and it is used widely in macro, development and trade. The conceptual contribution is simple and powerful.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow are the authors of the core framework. Restuccia and Rogerson, who made closely related contributions on policy distortions and productivity, are not in the credited list, and the list's names are limited to three. Attribution is good for the measurement framework, but the broader misallocation idea has several originators.
assessment.maturity: About fifteen years of influence. It has been widely applied but also debated, since measured misallocation can partly reflect measurement error or adjustment costs.
uncertainties: Concerns that measured dispersion in marginal products may reflect mismeasurement.
Omission of closely related work by others.
Possible preference for a method with more settled empirical standing.
My field proximity may bias me toward macro-growth topics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Empirical optimal taxation, built on taxable-income elasticities, sufficient-statistics methods and administrative data, changed how tax policy is analysed and evaluated. It links the theory of Mirrlees and Diamond to usable evidence and has had a strong effect on policy debate. The quality is very high.
assessment.attribution: Saez and Chetty are the most prominent in sufficient-statistics and tax-response work. Slemrod and Stantcheva are significant but have somewhat different contributions. Saez also appears under inequality (B044) and Chetty under mobility (B039), so credit is spread across several possible prizes.
assessment.maturity: Substantial, with twenty years of work. The core results are well replicated, but some of the most recent contributions are too new to judge fully.
uncertainties: Overlap between this candidate and B039 and B044 may dilute the case.
Possible concerns about age and timing relative to the strongest contributions.
Limited ability to compare the weight of Slemrod's earlier contribution with those of the proposed names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities is the basis of modern monetary policy analysis in central banks. Calvo pricing, the Taylor rule and Woodford's integration of the framework into a coherent theory of policy are foundational. The practical and intellectual influence is very large.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is hard because many people contributed: Calvo on staggered pricing, Taylor on rules and contracts, Woodford on the synthesis, and Gali, Gertler, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Smets on estimated models. A three-person limit forces difficult exclusions, which weakens the case compared with more tightly attributable candidates.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with decades of use in practice. Critiques after 2008 and the move toward heterogeneous-agent models have refined but not displaced it.
uncertainties: Severe attribution difficulty and risk of omitting key contributors.
Whether the committee judges the discovery as the framework or as individual building blocks.
Competing newer lines such as heterogeneous-agent models (B048), where I have a disclosed professional proximity through co-authorship with Violante.
